items.text: Bears TE Cole Kmet suffered a non-contact knee injury late in TNF win over Patriots, carted off, already ruled out; coach Ben Johnson said 'I don’t think it looked very good' with more tests Friday.
items.why: Non-contact knee, carted, coach pessimistic comment.
items.implication: Immediate TE volume shift in CHI offense; monitor diagnosis for multi-week absence.
items.opportunity: Increased routes/snaps/targets for remaining TEs especially in 12-personnel.

items.text: Rams WR Puka Nacua left practice early Thursday due to a calf injury and is listed as limited; severity unknown amid already thin WR room post-Adams IR.
items.why: Exited practice early with calf; listed limited on report.
items.implication: Game-time risk vs LV; if out or limited, massive target vacuum with Adams already sidelined 6-10 weeks.
items.opportunity: Elevated TE target share (previously 37% when Puka out) and backup WR snaps/routes.

items.text: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice officially didn’t practice for a second straight day due to his hamstring injury.
items.implication: Elevated risk of missing or being limited Week 7; monitor Friday report.
items.opportunity: Increased targets/routes for other KC WRs if sidelined.

items.text: Breece Hall back to practice (per Jets Thursday injury report).
items.why: Returned to practice after sitting Wednesday.
items.implication: Improving outlook for Week 7 availability vs MIA.
items.opportunity: Full snap/carry share if cleared; reduces handcuff urgency short-term.

items.text: Josh Jacobs allowed in team meetings, lifting, medical treatments and non-football activities at facility. MarShawn Lloyd (49th EPA/rush of 54) and Kaleb Johnson (53rd) have been quite bad (OL mess factor); discussed Jacobs long-term on ROS Top-150 show.
items.why: Facility access positive for return timeline; backups poor efficiency data.
items.implication: Jacobs ROS value supported if cleared soon; less trust in Lloyd/Johnson as standalones.
items.opportunity: Jacobs goal-line/early-down role intact long-term; monitor practice ramp.

items.text: Saquon Barkley is 'in line' to play vs DAL on MNF (Berry RB15); very efficient in two full games this season; Dallas one of best fantasy RB matchups.
items.why: Expected to return; prior efficiency + elite matchup.
items.opportunity: Full early-down/goal-line role vs soft DAL run D.

items.text: Notable: Terrance Ferguson (eligible off IR next week) not expected ready, recovery 'will take some time' per source. Biggest Adams beneficiary delayed; Rams' only answer now is 25 Puka Nacua targets per game.
items.why: Ferguson delay + Adams out forces hyper-concentrated targets on healthy Puka.
items.implication: Puka massive volume spike ROS until depth returns; calf now clouds it.
items.opportunity: 25+ target games possible; TE share also rises if Puka limited.
items.conflict: Conflicts with new calf injury limiting availability.

items.text: Bears D defended only 50 plays TNF (league-low avg 50.2/gm), allowed 0.48 pts/snap (would be 2nd-highest) and 7.6 yds/snap (worsens league-worst). Fraudulent D shielded by offense; +23 plays differential league-best.
items.why: Extreme positive plays differential and poor defensive efficiency driving offense volume.
items.implication: Sustained high snap/route volume for CHI pass-catchers/QB ROS.
items.opportunity: Elevated pace and scoring chances boost all skill players.

items.text: Loves A.J. Brown @ CHI (WR10): back in real role with 33% target share, 97% routes despite drops/3 catches for 27 yards in W6; Bears good yardage spot.
items.why: Elite route/target share + favorable matchup volume.
items.implication: Strong WR1/2 start; buy the usage rebound.
items.opportunity: High target share and red-zone potential vs soft Bears secondary.

items.text: Loves DeVonta Smith vs DAL (WR11): seeing elite volume in Eagles offense.
items.opportunity: Routes/targets elevated with other injuries possible.

items.text: Loves Tucker Kraft @ DET (TE6), Jaylen Warren @ NO (RB9), Chuba Hubbard vs TB (RB10), Bucky Irving @ CAR (RB12): big workloads in friendly matchups (Lions pass D gift; RB-friendly defenses).
items.why: Volume + matchup juice (DET soft vs pass catchers; carved-up run Ds).
items.implication: Strong starts across positions for volume plays.
items.opportunity: High snap/carry/target shares in positive game scripts.

items.text: Hates Rome Odunze vs NE (WR32), Josh Downs @ MIN (WR41), Travis Kelce @ SEA (TE9), Josh Jacobs @ DET (RB18), Cam Skattebo @ HOU (RB37): nasty matchups, role/target-share issues, workload questions post-layoff, or brutal spots.
items.why: Tough defenses, low target shares, return workload uncertainty.
items.implication: Sit or fade in favor of better volume/matchup options.
items.conflict: Jacobs facility access (Levitan) may support earlier return than pure hate implies.

items.text: Ashton Jeanty held under 3 YPC in 4 of past 5; two lowest snap rates past 2 weeks; Mike Washington season-high 33% snaps and only one fewer rush in W6. If inefficient, expect bigger Washington role.
items.why: Poor efficiency + declining snaps; backup rising.
items.implication: Jeanty flex risk; monitor split for handcuff value.
items.opportunity: Washington snap/carry growth if Jeanty limited.

items.text: Tough to ignore JJ McCarthy's 5.7 YPT when targeting Justin Jefferson (vs Mullens 10.8, Cousins 10.5, Darnold 10.0, Wentz 9.9). Different scheme/coaches/small sample but concerning; Giants plan to start McCarthy vs HOU.
items.why: Lowest YPT among recent QBs throwing to Jefferson.
items.implication: Jefferson efficiency/ceiling risk with McCarthy under center short-term.
items.opportunity: Volume still high but YAC/deep threat muted until chemistry improves.
